task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the largest gainer in an absent player's primary play types be identified from pre-absence initiation profiles?
How many absence spells or cases are needed to test whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer?
Do regression to the mean and selection of absences bias the estimated gains?

historical_evidence.finding: Tests connector absence against usage-matched non-organizer absence on team offensive identity (D_A). Unmatched connector vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97, p=2.87e-08. Usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35, p=7.35e-09, n=96. Versus terminal +0.0777, t=2.37, p=0.0261, n=25. Limited by small sample; risks MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER recorded.

Gravity persistence test of elite creators on teammate PPP at lags 1-3. All 8 creators at horizon 0; Jokic lag-1 ATT=+0.0282, CI[-0.043,+0.099], p=0.3779. Recorded as a clean null with adequate power (n=1880 for Jokic lag-1). A secondary Antetokounmpo distinct-initiator result (perm p=0.0002, BH 0.003) was marked as structure not effect, with the text cut.

Descriptive catalogue of same-player and teammate X->Y play-type sequence PPP premiums above baseline (e.g., P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560, n=31, t=+2.2; most cells recorded as DIRECT). Limited by label or classification error and small sample.

Exploratory position and Gobert sanity check on structural load using initiation totals. No result CSV or log was found; the verdict is recorded as abandoned, with failure type E_unclear and confidence low (0.15).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether elite creators' signature actions raise teammate PPP over subsequent possessions (lineup-matched, lags 1-3).
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null); no elite creator produced a positive lift at any lag. Shows that a gravity-style teammate-lift approach did not detect teammate gains in this data.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Exploratory group comparison of structural load by position and low initiation volume.
failed_approaches.why: No result was recorded; the output tables were not found and the mechanism is unclear (E_unclear). Abandoned.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Sequence-level premium estimates for play-type pairs.
failed_approaches.why: Mechanism unclear; limited by label or classification error and small cell sizes (n around 30-70), so premiums are not established as hypothesis tests.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work in this project has used the same play-by-play-derived initiation and PPP machinery and has found usage and identity effects of absence and connector roles ([prior work][prior work]).
A lineup-matched teammate-PPP lift from elite creators was not detected at any lag ([prior work][prior work]), so teammate gains in this framework are not a given.
Descriptive play-type sequence premiums exist but are small-sample and label-sensitive (FAM:[prior work]).
evidence_does_not_establish: Nothing retrieved tests whether the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types.
No retrieved record reports per-absence teammate gain rankings or a profile-similarity measure.
[prior work][prior work] measures team identity displacement (D_A), not teammate gains by play type, so it does not answer the ranking question.
The retrieved records do not establish how many absence cases are needed for a ranking test.
own_inferences: The effective sample for the question is 11 absence cases, not 148 spells. Spells from the same absent player are clustered, so the 148 spells overstate the information available for a ranking claim.
Among k candidate teammates, the largest gainer is roughly 1/k by chance. With 11 cases, a ranking test has very little power unless the effect is large.
Regression to the mean is a likely confounder: teammates with the most minutes or initiations may gain more because of exposure alone. Profile similarity is partly collinear with usage.
Initiation and profile measures are derived from the same play-by-play used to define the outcome, creating a label-dependence risk.
The 2025-26 season data are recorded as complete by 2026-11-01, but the playoff and regular-season splits and pre-absence windows may still mix regimes.
uncertainties: Definitions of 'closest profile', 'primary play types', and 'largest gainer' are not specified in the question.
The number of candidate teammates per absence and the size of the pre-absence window are not stated.
Whether absences are injuries, rests, or trades is not stated, which affects selection.
The retrieved records were truncated (marked [cut]), so the full text of [prior work][prior work] and FAM:[prior work] was not read.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved evidence reinforced the decision not to proceed as posed. The one supported absence study ([prior work][prior work]) answers a different outcome (identity displacement) and relied on a matched design with n=96, which the current 11-case unit cannot match. The teammate-lift null ([prior work][prior work]) and the abandoned structural-load study ([prior work][prior work]) show that teammate-gain and profile-based claims have not been established here, and that some prior exploratory analyses did not produce results.

blocking_constraints.text: Only 11 absence cases are available; a ranking test of the largest gainer has very low power against chance.
Many teammates have little exposure in the primary play types of each absent player, so gains are noisy or undefined.
Chance of picking the largest gainer among several teammates is about 1/k, so the baseline for success is low and must be stated.

prior_work.summary: None of the retrieved records tests whether the closest pre-absence initiation-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types. SF-[prior work] addresses absence effects on team identity (supported), SF-[prior work] reports a null teammate-PPP lift from elite creators (rejected), [prior work] is a descriptive sequence catalogue (not a hypothesis test), and SF-[prior work] has no result (abandoned). The question is partly adjacent to prior work but not answered by it.

risks.text: 11 absence cases give little power to rank teammates by gain; the 148 spells are clustered within those 11 players.
Teammates with few minutes or initiations in the primary play types produce unstable gain estimates.
Players selected as 'largest gainers' after an absence may simply have had high pre-absence usage and regress back toward their means.
Profile similarity, minutes, and same-position overlap are correlated, so the closest-profile effect cannot be separated from usage or role.
Initiation profiles and play-type gains are both derived from the play-by-play, so the profile and the outcome share a label source.
Play-type classification from action type and sub-type may be mislabeled, as noted for FAM:[prior work].
Single-season or short pre-absence windows give unreliable profile and gain measures.
The chance that the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer is about 1/k, so any hit rate must be compared to that baseline.
Scanning many play types and many candidate teammates per absence inflates false positives.
Rotations, pace, and roster changes across 2022-23 to 2025-26 and between regular season and playoffs can shift play-type usage.
[source]-database derivation of initiator and play-type records has not been validated against this question, so the pipeline needs checks before use.

design.estimand: As posed: the difference in primary play-type gain between the closest-profile teammate and the other teammates after an absence. Minimum viable: a descriptive estimate of how often the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer relative to the 1/k chance baseline, with uncertainty.
design.unit: Absence event (one absent player in one team-season), with teammates as candidate gainers within each event.
design.sample: Minimum viable: the 11 absence cases with their within-event teammate rankings. Do not treat the 148 spells as independent. Full test requires many more absence events than 11.
design.power: Not achievable with 11 cases for a ranking claim. Report the descriptive hit rate with a binomial or permutation interval against 1/k, and state that no power calculation supports a confirmatory claim.
design.controls: Regression to the mean (pre/post or within-player baseline), minutes and possession exposure, position, and absence reason. Profile similarity should be computed from a pre-absence window that does not overlap the outcome window.
design.falsification: The hypothesis is falsified if the closest-profile teammate is not the largest gainer more often than the 1/k chance baseline, using a permutation null that matches exposure and teammate set size.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary ranking statistic and one play-type definition. Correct for any additional play types or profile definitions with Benjamini-Hochberg or a permutation max-statistic.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a confirmatory test only if the design has at least the sample of absence events needed for the pre-specified power (to be computed before analysis) and the profile, outcome, and exposure windows are pre-registered and non-overlapping. Otherwise report only the descriptive result with stated limits.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, and 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as recorded complete on 2026-11-01 (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21). Frozen per-game files and the derived graph-database snapshot should be hashed and recorded before analysis.
